note: A list whose members are only known at runtime (issue #25). 2026-11-13: tried, not only read. A program declared with argenv 0.3.2 cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor more positionals than it names: a list needs a closed set of tokens, and only a list repeats. It is one need with three faces - snapall's --only declared as plain text (October, where this issue came from); an id typed from memory and refused three times in ocoeco's form (this week); and ocoeco's own --gathers, move TABLE ID..., and note --set, which cannot be declared at all. The three options in the issue ask how to permit free values; what the week showed is that the question is where values come from: declared (a closed set), asked (known only at runtime, and the program can tell them), or free (anything). 2026-11-13: designed (decision 2026-11-13-where-a-value-comes-from), prior art recorded (research where-values-come-from). When it lands, snapall's and lab-agent's own completion generators and oco-agent's hand-typed usage retire, and snapall's pinned test turns over: --only becomes a list whose members are asked. 2026-11-13, later the same day: the step designed here is held, not built. Seen from OCO's place (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry): what argenv declares is what a lens already declares, and asked is a relation. 2026-11-13, the trial in ocoeco: argenv's reader read a lens entry against records made as the program ran - nothing here had to change. What it showed lacking is not a field: the reader looks one way, taking words in; from a blank, what may enter is not yet answered anywhere but in ocoeco's form, and it needs what only the data knows - which rows exist.

note: Cause found 2026-11-09 by tracing every request the ADSP makes (a verbose hexagonrpcd build on the phone): the sensors service (hexagonrpcd -s) attaches the ADSP sensor process, whose registry init re-reads the sensor configs and needs to write (temp.json); hexagonrpcd refuses all writes, the firmware asserts (SNS_REG_INIT) and the whole ADSP restarts, taking audio with it. No registry state fixes it (packaged, or the phone own from persist, readable, with the version marker - which hexagonrpcd also never serves: a real gap, patch drafted). Fix in place on the phone: hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd masked. Result: 0 ADSP crashes across three boots and many minutes, the POCO X3 sound card up at about 12 s, playback without crashes. Trade-off: no ADSP sensors, which did not work anyway. Next: propose upstream (do not start sensorspd on surya until registry writes are supported; serve sns_reg_version in hexagonrpcd); see sensors-registry-writes. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed by masking the audio processor's helper services (hexagonrpcd rootpd, sensorspd).
title: The ADSP crashes every 13-25 s, restarting audio each time

note: Trigger found 2026-11-10, one change at a time: with hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper (a FastRPC client) attached, the audio DSP dies on every suspend attempt - 24 of 24 (fatal error EX:kernel:0x0:IST46:0x132:PC=0xf0049be4, about 30 ms after the attempt; the attempts abort at once because the USB link cannot go idle). Without the helper: 0 of 8, and on a clean boot with it masked 0 of 9, all checks passing; sound does not need it. Not a first-boot effect, not the sensor proxy, no stream open. The earlier "rare" crash (2 of 28, both early in a boot) was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down. Fixed in the lab: hexagonrpcd-adsp-rootpd masked in the device manifest, baked in at every flash. Still open, for upstream: why an attached FastRPC client makes the DSP assert across a suspend attempt (the kernel's fastrpc and remoteproc suspend handling, or hexagonrpcd), and why the helper restarts after each crash on a fresh system. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed with the same masks and the awake service.

Asked for 2026-11-10: the conveyor as a repo of its own, so anyone can bring support to another phone with the same conveyors, CI, tests, tad page and automatic integration into the grand picture; surya is the first instance, not the mould.

Design. (1) linux-phone-oco/device-template, a GitHub template repository: Use this template makes <vendor>-<codename>-lab. (2) device.toml, one manifest per device - codename, SoC, compatible strings, panel variants, image sources, how to reach the phone - read by every script; no script edited per device. (3) Generic machinery, generalized from surya-lab: the phone library (USB or Wi-Fi, commands on stdin), flashing with built-in fixes, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi from private files), switching shells, device-tree audits, an upstream queue with send commands generated by get_maintainer.pl. (4) Tests as small independent checks, one file each declaring its component and what it needs, so a device runs the checks that apply; results as JSON lines with a versioned schema. (5) Device-independent analysis in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools (Rust): tone (speaker tests microphone) first. (6) Onboarding conveyor: a lab-tools command reads a running phone (compatible, inputs, outputs, sound devices) and fills device.toml - and from the same facts generates the Sxmo device profile. (7) Each device repo publishes its own tad data (support status, test runs, wiki claims) with CI that validates it and renders its page. (8) Integration: a feed in linux-phone-oco/docs discovers device repos by a GitHub topic and pulls their published tables, so a new device appears in the devices table and the support grid (tad draws device x component as a matrix) with no hand edits. (9) Conventions in AGENTS.md: explicit intent for state changes, lists as arguments, secrets outside repos, fingerprints before trusting images. (10) Proof: surya-lab re-based onto the template as its first instance - still 18 of 18 through it. Landscape read 2026-11-10 (see the landscape table): build on what exists - device.toml derives from postmarketOS deviceinfo; tests take the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI tests and use bootrr for driver probes; the lab aims to be a CI-tron-compatible setup and surya a device under test in pmOS's hardware farm; flashing leans on pmbootstrap.

note: Plasma Mobile (fresh Nura image, sound fixes applied on the phone): speakers were silent with the whole chain playing. Two causes, both confirmed: (1) the image restores a saved mixer state with both amplifiers' digital volume at 0 = -110 dB; (2) a tas2562 driver bug: setting the Digital Volume Control changes only the driver's cache, the chips (page 2, 0x0c-0x0f) stay at -110 dB. Writing 0x40000000 straight into both chips with i2cset made sound work: the user heard YouTube in Firefox, 2026-11-10. Not persistent: after a power-off the restore and the driver bug bring the silence back. Needed: the driver fix (upstream-tas2562-volume), and until then a boot-time step that writes the volume into the chips. Root cause found and fixed 2026-11-10: the tas2562 driver's maximum volume (0 dB) read past the end of its lookup table, which muted the amps; with two more faults (the latch byte written first, resume skipping bytes). Fixed module installed and proven on the phone by I2C reads; every flash bakes it in. Listen on Plasma when it is next run.
